message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| **Physical State (298 K, 1 atm)** | State | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (−423.17 °F) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (−434.69 °F) |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat (Cp) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.449 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Speed of sound | ~1270 m s⁻¹ (in H₂) |
| | Refractive index | 1.000132 (at 589 nm) |
| | Viscosity | 8.76 × 10⁻⁶ Pa·s |
| | Thermal conductivity | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (H₂) |
| | Bonding | Forms covalent bonds; H₂ is a diatomic molecule with a single σ bond |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids with nonmetals |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (H⁺ donor) in aqueous solution; forms hydronium (H₃O⁺) |
| | Combustion | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Redox potential | Standard reduction potential for H⁺/H₂: 0 V (by definition) |
| | Solubility in water | ~0.0006 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C (very low) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Good in nonpolar solvents (e.g., hexane, benzene) |
| | Spectroscopic features | 1s→2p transition at 121.6 nm (Lyman‑α line); Raman shift ~ 4155 cm⁻¹ |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Most abundant (~99.98 %) |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable isotope; heavier, used in NMR, D₂O (“heavy water”) |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (β⁻ emitter, half‑life 12.32 y); used in nuclear fusion research |
| **Applications & Roles** | Fuel source | Hydrogen fuel cells, rocket propellant |
| | Industrial | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, hydrogenation reactions |
| | Energy carrier | Potential for large‑scale energy storage (e.g., grid‑level) |
| | Astrophysics | Primary element in stars; fusion in the Sun (pp‑chain) |
| | Analytical chemistry | Used as a reducing agent in chromatography, as a carrier gas in mass spectrometry |
| | Environmental | Clean combustion produces only water; key in reducing CO₂ emissions |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: atomic number 1, mass ~1 u.
- **Diatomic gas**: H₂ is the most stable form under normal conditions.
- **Highly reactive**: readily forms hydrides, acids, and fuels.
- **Isotopic diversity**: protium, deuterium, tritium each with distinct physical/chemical behavior.
- **Energy relevance**: central to both stellar fusion and future clean‑energy technologies.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
